title: Bind wagon produce/consume contracts to registered contract identities

facts.note: Wagon manifests carry the produce/consume graph; the registry is the single source of truth for contract identities.

values: contract field changed (including set to null)
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer over YAML produce/consume entries and registry keys.
Reviewing or validating an existing wagon graph also activates the rule, even with no edit, since the invariants hold over the whole graph.
Produced by the coherence validator test_contract_registry_coherence; requires the validator output to be surfaced as a fact. Any finding on the existing graph activates the rule.
Planning tasks touching wagon interfaces or contracts.

fires: A planner adds a consume entry whose contract: URN strips to an identity not present in contracts/_contracts.yaml.
A planner adds a produce entry for an artifact name that another wagon consumes, with contract: null.
A produce entry declares a non-null contract that no other wagon consumes and is not marked to: external.
A contract is renamed or removed from the registry while wagon manifests still reference its URN.

A planner reviews or validates existing wagon manifests that already contain an unregistered URN, a null-contract cross-wagon producer, or an unconsumed non-external produced contract — even without editing them.
doesNotFire: NULL-CROSS-WAGON only: a produce entry with contract: null whose artifact name is not consumed by any other wagon is exempt from NULL-CROSS-WAGON; the rule is inactive only if UNREGISTERED and UNCONSUMED also hold for the rest of the graph.

UNCONSUMED only: a produced contract consumed by no wagon but explicitly marked to: external is exempt from UNCONSUMED; its URN must still resolve to a registered identity (UNREGISTERED), and NULL-CROSS-WAGON must still hold elsewhere.
Edits to wagon manifest fields unrelated to produce/consume (e.g. descriptions) that leave contract bindings unchanged — only when the graph already satisfies all three invariants.
Changes outside plan/ wagon manifests and the contract registry, when the existing graph already satisfies all three invariants.

given: Wagon manifests (plan/<wagon>/_<wagon>.yaml) declare produce/consume entries; contracts/_contracts.yaml is the single source of truth for each contract's identity, path, theme, producers and consumers.
when: You author, change, review or validate produce/consume entries, their contract: fields, or registry entries.
then: Every non-null contract: URN on a produce or consume entry must, after stripping the contract: prefix, resolve to an identity registered in contracts/_contracts.yaml.
prefer: Add new contract identities to the registry through its authoring flow (create_contract), so the registry entry carries identity, path, theme, producers and consumers.
Mandatory (NULL-CROSS-WAGON): give the producing entry of every cross-wagon edge (artifact name produced by one wagon, consumed by a different wagon) a non-null registered contract.
Mandatory (UNCONSUMED): mark a produced non-null contract that no other wagon consumes as to: external.
avoid: URNs whose identity, after stripping the contract: prefix, is absent from the registry (typos, renamed or deleted contracts). A prefixed URN is valid when its stripped identity is a registry key.
contract: null on a cross-wagon producer (dangling producer, no contract binds the edge) — a required invariant, not optional.
A produced non-null contract no other wagon consumes and not marked to: external — a required invariant, not optional.
Silencing findings by nulling contract: or adding to: external to an internally consumed contract.
unless: A produced contract with no consuming wagon is coherent if marked to: external (exempts UNCONSUMED only).
why: The registry owns contract identity and producer/consumer ownership; unregistered URNs, null-bound cross-wagon edges and orphan producers let plan graph and registry drift.
evidence: test_contract_registry_coherence::test_contract_registry_coherence passes with no UNREGISTERED, NULL-CROSS-WAGON or UNCONSUMED findings (all three invariants are required).
Reviewer can map each contract: URN in the wagon manifests, after stripping the contract: prefix, to a key in contracts/_contracts.yaml.
Each cross-wagon edge has a non-null contract on its producing entry; each produced non-null contract has another consuming wagon or to: external.
verifier_detail: Registry keys are contract identities; strip the 'contract:' URN prefix before lookup.
UNREGISTERED: every non-null contract: URN on any produce or consume entry must strip to an existing registry identity.

NULL-CROSS-WAGON: cross-wagon edges are keyed on artifact NAME — a name produced by one wagon and consumed by a different wagon; the producing entry must declare a non-null contract (contract: null there = dangling producer). Same-wagon produce/consume is not a cross-wagon edge.
UNCONSUMED: every produce entry with a non-null contract must be consumed by at least one OTHER wagon or carry to: external.

Three invariants are checked across the whole graph: plan/<wagon>/_<wagon>.yaml produce/consume entries of all wagons against contracts/_contracts.yaml. Exemptions are per-invariant (no cross-wagon edge exempts only NULL-CROSS-WAGON; to: external exempts only UNCONSUMED).

additions.text: Source bundles three independent invariants (UNREGISTERED, NULL-CROSS-WAGON, UNCONSUMED). UNREGISTERED kept as then; the other two placed in prefer/avoid/unless/verifier_detail (explicitly labelled mandatory) and proposed as separate conventions planner.contract.no-null-cross-wagon-producer and planner.contract.produced-has-consumer.
additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation per then; labels prevent the mandatory invariants from being read as optional preferences.

additions.text: prefer[0]: add new contract identities through the registry's authoring flow (create_contract). No edit-ordering is prescribed; only the resulting graph/registry state matters.
additions.justification: Source (S024) names create_contract as the registry's authoring flow; phrased as a pointer, not a sequencing requirement.
